basis: DOK7-related neuromuscular junction disorder; weakness, ptosis and respiratory muscle insufficiency do not establish separate muscle, eye or lung damage.
Inherited cerebellar ataxia; the parent establishes neurologic disease despite the empty definition.
Manganese neurotoxicity with dystonia affects most patients across both listed subtypes; cirrhosis and polycythemia are subtype-specific.
MNGIE defines metabolic, neural and intestinal disease; ophthalmoplegia/ptosis occur in nearly 100%. Myopathy and hearing loss (14/31) omitted because of the cap.
Benign adipose neoplasm arising in the colorectal wall.
Defined as isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; SGCD association alone does not establish skeletal muscle disease.
Epiphyseal and joint dysplasia define the disease; tooth agenesis occurs in only 1/4 patients.
Structural defect of the vertebral pars interarticularis.
Developmental brain disease, cleft palate (60%) and clubfeet define the syndrome; nail hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac frequency unclear; lung hypoplasia 2/7 excluded.
Isolated familial dilated cardiomyopathy; PSEN1 does not establish neurologic involvement in this concept.
Mitochondrial complex I disorder; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 2/2 and encephalopathy in 1/1 annotated patients support involvement, with small samples.
Calcium metabolism disorder; organ injury is not universal across its heterogeneous causes and severities.
Neoplasm originates in the small intestine; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Laryngeal dysfunction directly compromises the upper airway; no established common additional organ damage.
MELAS is a mitochondrial encephalomyopathy; sensorineural hearing loss affects roughly half of MELAS patients, although MT-TC-specific frequency data are limited.
Carcinoma in situ confined to the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Ocular refractive disorder producing unequal perceived image size or shape.
Complex I deficiency with developmental and neurologic dysfunction and optic atrophy in 1/1 annotated patients. Central hypoventilation does not establish lung disease.
The defining triad comprises laryngeal atresia, encephalocele and structural limb deformities.
SEC63 polycystic liver disease is supported by the parent and hepatic cyst phenotypes; the kidney wording in the definition conflicts with this evidence.
Elongated styloid process or calcified stylohyoid ligament defines the lesion; otalgia and dysphagia are symptoms, while vascular injury is not common across the syndrome.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with retinal atrophy and visual loss.
Malignant neoplasm originating in the lung; mesenchymal differentiation does not establish skeletal involvement.
Generalized GALE deficiency commonly causes liver dysfunction, developmental impairment and cataracts (approximately >=30% each); this excludes the benign peripheral form.
Systemic sclerosis causes autoimmune skin fibrosis; esophageal dysfunction affects ~80% and interstitial lung disease ~40-60%. Familial-specific frequencies are unavailable.
